lens: CLAIMS (round 2). I re-checked the claims new in this revision against primary sources on 2026-10-15. Sources read: ds4 SSD_STREAMING.md, PERFORMANCE.md, METAL.md, MODELS.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md, plus the GitHub commit API for speed-bench/m5_max.csv; AtomicChat dsv4-eval-artifacts (README and all four results JSONL files); GSQ arXiv 2604.18556 (full text through orx), the GSQ GitHub README and the ISTA-DASLab K2.6 GSQ card; arXiv 2609.25809, 2609.04575, 2608.07911, 2610.02241, 2509.25689 and 2609.18110 (orx full text); the six Kimi K3 pruned-build cards; the sombra-x, ubicloud and mradermacher cards; the Ex0bit and kwanhee cards; the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 card and API metadata; the Artificial Analysis pages for GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and V4.1 Flash; Hugging Face tree sums for 15 cited files; the antirez HF listings; flash-moe CLAUDE.md; SGLang expert_distribution.py; the vLLM docker and context-parallel docs; llama.cpp PRs #24162, #29887 and #25294; ik_llama.cpp PR #239; the Cerebras REAP README and HF listing; the stared README; the Weschera README; the Computerworld article; oMLX runs ez6mnyny, 8y9ori5i, 93kgjkbc, qsgif005 and jw1099pr; Simon Willison's streaming-experts post; local `df -H`, `sysctl` and `headroom status`; and the main repo's kimi-k26-fetch evidence (commit 90c337f5). Confirmed as written: every ds4 M5 Max streaming number (S109) and every Flash Q2 baseline number (S95); S136's date; all AtomicChat KLD and top-1 rows cited; all GSQ task numbers (Tables 3, 6, 10, 13 and 14) and the card's facts (293.97 GB, Humming format, Hopper or Ampere); the Nota and mlx reap160 numbers; the S119 V4 Flash numbers (75.69 → 74.53; 165B / 11.5B); S120's 2.10 → 0.55; the S121 override flag; the K2.6 router config; the S122 recorder facts (top-8 buffer, TBO assert, fusion TODO); the S124 quotes; the S118 merge date; S132 (HTTP 404) and S131 (HTTP 401); all S133 and S134 sizes; the AA scores and parameter counts; the flash-moe figures; MoESQ's 43,810 and 42,580 characters; S22's "over 5 tokens/s" and 6 of 192 experts; and S41's GLM-5.3-Flash PCIe 4 comment.

problems.claim: Sec 1: 'Kimi K3 builds with more than 50% of their experts removed keep their coding ability but lose factual recall [S113]... A 100 GB Kimi would at best be a coding specialist.' Row K6: 'Kimi K3 builds pruned 80-82% keep code but fail factual recall.' G1: 'the 80-82% builds keep coding but fail factual recall.'
problems.problem: This overgeneralizes thin evidence, and it is wrong for one of the two builds it names. The 80% build (pipenetwork REAP80, MXFP4 experts kept bit-exact) answers the France probe correctly. Only the 82% build fails it, and that build is also requantized to 2-bit, so pruning and quantization are confounded. The coding evidence for both builds is one greedy completion of one function. No coding benchmark exists above 50% pruning.
problems.evidence: pipenetwork/Kimi-K3-REAP80-MLX-mxfp4-q8 card (read 2026-10-15), verbatim greedy sample: prompt 'The capital of France is' gives 'Paris.' followed by list-like drift; the Chinese prompt loops. mlx-community/Kimi-K3-mlx-reap160-2bit card: 160 of 896 experts, 2-bit affine; France prompt loops; its evidence is one 40-token greedy run each of merge_intervals, France and Chinese; 'perplexity / benchmarks: not done'. The only K3 coding benchmark is at 50% (Nota card: HumanEval+ 82.32 / 82.32 / 81.71).
problems.fix: Restate as follows. At 50% (REAP or Nota), GPQA-D falls 17-20 points while HumanEval+ holds. At 80% with native MXFP4 experts, single prompts show drift and Chinese loops, but the factual probe is answered. At 82% plus 2-bit, the factual probe fails. Coding above 50% rests on one prompt per build. Add mgoin's GSM8K series (next finding) as the quantitative knowledge-loss evidence. Soften 'keep their coding ability'.

problems.claim: Sec 1 and A5: 'Purpose-built streamers reach about 5.85-10.6 GB/s, so each GB that misses the cache costs 94-171 ms.' This range is used for every Kimi streaming estimate (2.5-5.8 tok/s). A5 and sec 3b: 'llama.cpp is up to 2.82 times slower than SSD-LLaMA'; 'up to 2.82 times faster than llama.cpp and 1.93 times faster than KTransformers'.
problems.problem: The 5.85-10.6 GB/s range is not a measured number for any Mac. It applies SSD-LLaMA's Linux and CUDA percentages (43-78%) to a 4 TB reviewer figure, yet section 1 states it as fact. The only purpose-built macOS streamer the dossier quantifies (flash-moe) implies about 3.4 GB/s (A5), below the floor. The ds4 back-tests cannot separate h from B (A6's own conclusion). Separately, 2.82× and 1.93× are ratios of SSD read bandwidth, not of speed. SSD-LLaMA's end-to-end decode speedups are 1.35-3.44× over llama.cpp and 1.57-15.61× over KTransformers.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2609.18110 §5.2: 'SSD-LLaMA consistently achieves significantly higher read bandwidth than llama.cpp and KTransformers... SSD-LLaMA delivers up to 2.82× and 1.93× speedups over llama.cpp and KTransformer' (paragraph on read bandwidth); same section: 'In the decoding stage, SSD-LLaMA achieves a 1.35×–3.44× speedup over llama.cpp and a 1.57×–15.61× speedup over KTransformers.' flash-moe CLAUDE.md: 'parallel pread K=4 experts [2.41ms SSD]', page cache '~71% hit rate'. Dossier A5 derives 3.4 GB/s from these.
problems.fix: In section 1, label 5.85-10.6 GB/s as an assumption carried over from a Linux testbed. Add the flash-moe-derived 3.4 GB/s as a low case and show the K2 estimate at that bandwidth. Call 2.82× and 1.93× read-bandwidth ratios, and quote the decode speedups separately.

problems.claim: Sec 1: 'GSQ, a CUDA-only 2.13-bit format'. Sec 3a Limits: GSQ is among methods that are 'CUDA-first, not Metal-first'; '...which is CUDA-only'. G1(a): the GGUF imatrix route 'gives only a lower bound... GSQ beat Unsloth's k-quants'. G1(b): GSQ costs 190-250 H100 GPU-hours per configuration.
problems.problem: This holds for the published Humming checkpoint only, not for the method. The paper (§4.4) and the repository say GSQ refines GGUF K-quant checkpoints in their own format, and the result 'runs unchanged on llama.cpp / Ollama'. A GSQ-refined GGUF is therefore a Mac-runnable route that G1 omits, though it is tested only on dense Qwen3-8B and 4B. Also omitted: the GSQ repository lists Kimi K2/K2.5 as needing '8× H100/H200 (full node) minimum, typically 1–2 nodes'. That collides with GPU 0 being held until 2026-10-21. Smaller points: the Kimi AgentBench comparison is against UD-IQ1_M, an i-quant rather than a k-quant, and it used a 2.37-bit GSQ configuration, not the 2.13-bit checkpoint.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2604.18556 §4.4: 'GSQ treats the GGUF checkpoint as the initialization point... projects the result back into the same format... remains compatible with standard GGUF inference stacks'; Table 14 'Unsloth_UD-IQ1_M (2.4bit)' vs 'GSQ (2.37bit)'. github.com/IST-DASLab/GSQ README: 'directly compatible with existing INT inference kernels and with GGUF K-Quant deployment stacks'; 'the optimized checkpoint runs unchanged on llama.cpp / Ollama'; 'Kimi-K2.5 ... 8× H100/H200 (full node), typically 1–2 nodes'.
problems.fix: Say that the K2.6 GSQ checkpoint is CUDA-only, while GSQ-in-GGUF is Metal-compatible but tested only on dense Qwen3. Add a G1 configuration (c): GSQ refinement of a Kimi GGUF K-quant, if the repository's K-quant path supports this MoE. State GSQ's full-node requirement and schedule it after 2026-10-21. Name UD-IQ1_M as an i-quant at 2.37 bits.

problems.claim: Sec 3c table: 'mgoin pruned75 (no calibration) | 224 of 896 | 475 GB | GSM8K 34.42% (5-shot; no base score on the card)'. Sec 3c Limits: 'Community Kimi K3 builds pruned 50-82% exist in MLX and GGUF, with qualitative failure reports and no benchmarks [S113].' S113 read level: mgoin card 'full'.
problems.problem: The mgoin card does give base scores, measured on the same harness: source K3 95.53% and pruned50 68.23%. These are the strongest quantitative knowledge-loss numbers for G1's prior, and the dossier omits them. 'No benchmarks' also contradicts the dossier's own Nota row and prometheusAIR's needle test.
problems.evidence: huggingface.co/mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75 card: 'Kimi-K3-pruned75 34.4200% 454/1319 | Kimi-K3-pruned50 68.2335% 900/1319 | Source Kimi-K3 95.5269% 1260/1319', all on the same harness, hardware and seed. prometheusAIR/Kimi-K3-REAP55-GGUF card: 'needle test 15/15 exact through 64K'; decode 0.48 tok/s warm when streaming from NVMe.
problems.fix: Replace 'no base score' with 95.53 → 68.23 (50%) → 34.42 (75%), calibration-free, 5-shot GSM8K. Add these to G1's prior. Reword the Limits line to say that benchmarks are few and mostly from the makers.

problems.claim: G2 / What to measure: replay event by event ('event-atomic'): 'sequential replay inflated LRU hit rates by 27.4%' [S123].
problems.problem: The direction is inverted. In S123, sequential replay inflates the LRU miss fraction by 27.4%: it counts artificial refetches, so it understates hit rates. The figure is also specific to Qwen3-30B-A3B at ρ=40% and B=8.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2608.07911 Table 2: 'LRU 24.59% [sequential] 19.30% [event-atomic] +27.4%' under 'Effective miss fraction under sequential and event-atomic replay. (128-expert model... ρ = 40%, B = 8)'; §1: 'sequential replay inflates LRU by 27.4%... an artificial refetch'.
problems.fix: Write: 'sequential replay inflated the LRU miss fraction by 27.4% (Qwen3-30B-A3B, 40% resident, 8 concurrent), so it understates hit rates.' Check whether S82's LRU numbers used sequential replay before treating A7's brackets as pessimistic or optimistic.

problems.claim: Sec 1: 'Kimi has no supported streaming engine on the Mac and only one community report (about 1.7 tokens/s on a 128 GB M4 Max)'; 'No purpose-built Metal streamer for Kimi K2 is documented.' Row K2: 'The only report on a Mac this size is about 1.7 tokens/s'.
problems.problem: A documented MLX pread-based SSD streamer has run Kimi-K2 on a 128 GB Mac. It is a small experiment, but it contradicts 'only one report' and 'no ... documented'. The 1.7 tok/s report's engine and quant are also not stated in S51 itself.
problems.evidence: github.com/rita-aga/mlx-turboquant-moe-streaming README (created 2026-03-26): 'We ran Kimi-K2 (1.04 trillion parameters, 578 GB on disk) on an M3 Max MacBook Pro with 128 GB RAM. It used 7.1 GB of RAM'; results table 'Kimi-K2 | 1.04T | 578 GB | 7.1 GB | 0.5 tok/s'; streaming via 'pread()' with MLX. Simon Willison's post (2026-03-24) names no engine or quant for the 1.7 tok/s report.
problems.fix: Add this report: Kimi-K2 MLX 4-bit, 128 GB M3 Max, about 7 GB resident, 0.5 tok/s, experimental code. Reword to 'no maintained or supported Metal streamer for Kimi K2'.

problems.claim: Sec 1, sec 4 and sec 5 (three places): 'K2.6 INT4 (595 GB) is being downloaded to the host now'; host file list: 'K2.6 INT4: 595.3 (downloading)'.
problems.problem: This is stale. The main repository's evidence, committed before this dossier was saved (13:37), records a completed fetch that matched the Hub file for file. The received bytes are 595.2 GB.
problems.evidence: /Users/kevinliu/repos/cotcodec commit 90c337f5 (2026-10-15 12:55 -0700), program/evidence/2026-10-16/kimi-k26-fetch/README.md: 'job 1528... ended COMPLETED 0:0 after 55 min 36 s... 96 files and 595,204,999,341 bytes... matches the Hub's own listing file for file, including all 67 LFS SHA-256 values.' The same file confirms the GPU 0 hold (transcreate-lama, D110, until 2026-10-21).
problems.fix: Replace with 'K2.6 INT4 is on the host (job 1528, 595.2 GB, receipt in kimi-k26-fetch)' and cite that evidence folder.

problems.claim: Row F1 (labelled 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731'): 'community report: a ds4 q2–q4 mix (91 GB file, 103 GB in use), 33 / 28 decode [S96]'; 'A 128 GB M4 Max ran it with about 103 GB wired and no growth in swap [S108]'. Conflict 12: '284B / 13B on its card'. Sec 3b recipe: 'DeepSeek Flash MXFP4, 156 GB'.
problems.problem: Checkpoint mixing survives the CL-06 fix. S96's run is dated 2026-06-14, before 0731 existed (created 2026-07-31), so it is not the 0731 checkpoint. S108 is the Vision-Exp checkpoint, and its 103 GB wired figure is at 1M context. The 0731 card does not state 284B / 13B (the April card does). The recipe's '156 GB MXFP4' does not say Vision-Exp. A reader would download ds4f-mxfp4 (0731, also 155.98 GB), which is not the measured file.
problems.evidence: stared README: 'median of 3 runs · 2026-06-14'. HF API deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 createdAt 2026-07-31. Weschera README title 'DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision-Exp on a Mac Studio'; 'At 1M the Mac sits at ~103 GB wired... swap flat'. 0731 README has no parameter count; the April README says '284B parameters (13B activated)'. antirez/deepseek-v4-gguf lists both '...MXFP4...-0731.gguf' and 'Vision-Exp-MXFP4...gguf' at 155.98 GB.
problems.fix: Label S96 as the April checkpoint, and S108 as Vision-Exp (same file size; at 1M context). Cite the April card for 284B / 13B. In the recipe, name the target as 'ds4f-vision-mxfp4 (Vision-Exp; the file ds4 measured)'.

problems.claim: Sec 3b and row K2: prefill '84-155 if the whole prompt passes through each layer in one batch (as ds4 does)'; 'ds4 sends large prompts through each layer in wide batches and overlaps reads with compute on Metal [S110]'. Sec 1: 'a 30,000-token prompt takes about 3-12 minutes'.
problems.problem: ds4 does not say it passes the whole prompt in one batch for the V4 Flash or GLM files measured. The 'wide batches' and Metal-overlap sentence appears only in MODELS.md's V4.1 Flash section. PERFORMANCE.md gives 4,096-token default chunks for ordinary DeepSeek and graph-selected chunks for GLM. Labelling 84-155 tok/s 'ds4 style' is therefore an inference, and the 3-minute lower bound of section 1 rests on it.
problems.evidence: ds4 docs/PERFORMANCE.md: 'Prefill defaults are configuration-specific: ordinary DeepSeek uses 4096-token chunks, CUDA TP uses 2048, and long PRO prompts may use 8192. GLM chooses its own chunks'. docs/MODELS.md (under 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash'): 'Large SSD prefills process layers in wide batches. Metal overlaps computation with the next layer's reads'. QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md: 'warm-SSD matrix-prefill threshold at 1024 tokens'.
problems.fix: Call the whole-prompt case a bound, not 'ds4 style'. Cite the documented 4,096-token default and state the 30K prefill range with it, which gives 6.5-12 min by the dossier's own table. Scope the overlap sentence to V4.1 Flash, or confirm it in the ds4 source.

problems.claim: Sec 4 / G4: 'AtomicChat ladder... about 30 quants of the 0731 checkpoint, all measured on one machine'; sec 3a: 'the same file's perplexity differs by 4-5% between RTX 5090 and H100'. Sec 3e: '98.8% on average across 12 checkpoints [S119]'. G5: the authors call standard renormalization 'the worst choice' [S120].
problems.problem: These are several small misstatements of their sources. AtomicChat's README says the rival-publisher results are 'split by the machine that produced them' (B1-B3), and the ds4 Q2 row comes from RIVALS-B3; about 47 quant rows were measured, not 30. The 4-5% perplexity gap is for the BF16 reference model. S119's 98.8% averages nine models, not twelve checkpoints. S120's wording is 'precisely the setting we find worst on both models', not 'the worst choice'.
problems.evidence: AtomicChat README: 'RIVALS-B1.jsonl, RIVALS-B2.jsonl, RIVALS-B3.jsonl | Parsed results, other publishers, split by the machine that produced them'; 'Same file, same corpus, same commit, reference model: RTX 5090 4.5381 / H100 4.3406'. arXiv 2609.25809 §4.1: 'preserves 98.8% of unpruned performance, averaged over nine models and three task families'. arXiv 2609.04575 §2: 'precisely the setting we find worst on both models'.
problems.fix: Say 'about 47 quants, on 8× RTX 5090 machines (rival files split by machine)'; 'the BF16 reference's perplexity differs 4-5%'; '98.8% averaged over nine models'. Paraphrase S120 without quotation marks.

problems.claim: Sec 3c Limits: 'GGUFs of a layer-truncated K2.5 (the first 20 of 61 layers), which its maker describes as "intended for pipeline testing"' [S137].
problems.problem: The GGUF does not exist in that form. mradermacher's GGUF is of ubicloud/Kimi-K2.5-BF16-Pruned-20B, which keeps the first 2 of 61 layers. The 20-layer variant (ubicloud/Kimi-K2.5-Pruned-340B) is safetensors only.
problems.evidence: ubicloud/Kimi-K2.5-BF16-Pruned-20B card: 'retains the first 2 layer(s) of the original 61 layer(s)'. mradermacher/Kimi-K2.5-BF16-Pruned-20B-GGUF: 'static quants of https://huggingface.co/ubicloud/Kimi-K2.5-BF16-Pruned-20B'; files 7.7-21.2 GB. ubicloud/Kimi-K2.5-Pruned-340B: 'retains the first 20 layer(s)', no GGUF.
problems.fix: Write: 'GGUFs of a 2-layer truncation of K2.5 (mradermacher, from ubicloud's BF16-Pruned-20B), intended for pipeline testing.'

problems.claim: A2: 'Kimi K2.6 DQ3_K_M on an M3 Ultra (819 GB/s)... about 18 GB per token × 21.7 tokens/s = about 390 GB/s, so e ≈ 0.48' (no citation).
problems.problem: The figure has no citation. It comes from oMLX run qsgif005 [S46], an MLX build named 'Kimi-K2.6DQ3_K_M-q8' and labelled '4bit', with a peak memory of 439.6 GB. It is not a GGUF DQ3_K_M. Its 'q8' label conflicts with assuming an Unsloth-like spine of 8.5 GB, and other runs of the same build give 20.3-22.0.
problems.evidence: omlx.ai/benchmarks/qsgif005: Kimi-K2.6DQ3_K_M-q8, '4bit', M3 Ultra 512 GB, oMLX v0.4.1, 1k TG 21.7, PP 222.2, peak 439.6 GB (2026-06-06). Runs 8y9ori5i: 22.0; 93kgjkbc: 20.8; ez6mnyny: 20.3.
problems.fix: Cite S46 (qsgif005), say it is an MLX build, give 20.3-22.0 across runs, and take the bytes per token from its 439.6 GB footprint and q8 spine rather than from Unsloth's spine.

problems.claim: G4: the S131 card reports 'a 7-benchmark average of 78.09 → 69.85 (about −8 points) and MMLU 82.10 → 59.60' (unverified; HTTP 401). F1: 'about −8 points for a 90.9 GiB mixed Q2 file'.
problems.problem: This is still unverifiable, and the search summaries disagree. A search on 2026-10-15 describes the card as six benchmarks: the oQ2.5e MLX build at 74.56 vs 78.09, and the 90.9 GiB 'Q4K+IQ2XXS' GGUF at 69.85. Which checkpoint (April or 0731) is not stated. G4's pre-registered expectation rests on these numbers.
problems.evidence: curl https://huggingface.co/Jundot/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-oQ2.5e-mtp gives 401 (2026-10-15). WebSearch summary: 'Across six benchmarks, the quantized version averages 74.56%, against 78.09%... a GGUF Q4K+IQ2XXS build at 90.9 GiB averaging 69.85%'. 90.9 GiB matches antirez's 97.59 GB Layers37-42 Q4K mix (ds4f-q2-q4), not ds4 Q2.
problems.fix: Drop the benchmark count and the MMLU pair unless the card is read. Say the file is the ds4f-q2-q4 mix with an unknown checkpoint. Keep G4's expectation only as a weak prior.

problems.claim: Assorted: sec 5 'Its README warns that a macOS virtual-memory bug can crash the kernel on the CPU path [S95]'; A5 'Reviewers measured... 12.7 GB/s (PetaPixel, Blackmagic test)... [S3, S4]'; sec 3c 'Cerebras REAP checkpoints for... None for Kimi [S61]'; row G2 'BF16 checkpoints only'.
problems.problem: These are small citation errors. The ds4 warning is in CONTRIBUTING.md, not the README, and it names 'a kernel bug in macOS'. Computerworld [S3] measured 12.59 GB/s read, while 12.7 is PetaPixel's figure. Cerebras publishes Kimi-Linear-REAP-35B, so the statement should be 'none for Kimi K2'. Cerebras also publishes FP8 builds of the GLM-4.6 REAP checkpoints.
problems.evidence: ds4 CONTRIBUTING.md: 'executing the CPU path on Metal can crash the system because of a kernel bug in macOS'; README.md has no such text. Computerworld: 'Blackmagic's Disk Speed Test returns a phenomenal 12,587.3 MBps read speed' (4 TB, 128 GB). HF API author=cerebras: Kimi-Linear-REAP-35B-A3B-Instruct; GLM-4.6-REAP-218B/252B/268B-A32B-FP8.
problems.fix: Cite CONTRIBUTING.md; write 'Computerworld 12.6, PetaPixel 12.7, The Verge 13.6'; 'none for Kimi K2'; 'BF16 and FP8 checkpoints'.

round1_fixes_confirmed:
I checked all 23 round-1 claims findings (CL-01 to CL-23) against the revised text and the sources.
- Fixed and verified at source: CL-01 (ds4 SSD_STREAMING numbers, dates and caveats match exactly), CL-02 (113.38 GB, 105.6 GiB, 1.79 bpw; the 130 GB scores are attributed to unpruned DeepSeek-V3), CL-03 (vllm-private still 404), CL-05 (235.09 GB smol-IQ1_KT for K2-0905, K2.5 and K2.6; K2.5 UD-TQ1_0 239.54 GB), CL-07, CL-10 (stared table: 93/85, 105/85, 18/17, 17/17), CL-11, CL-12, CL-13, CL-14, CL-15 (the PCIe 4 GLM-5.3-Flash comment exists), CL-16, CL-17, CL-18, CL-19, CL-20 (Instruct and 0905 are 1,029 GB; Thinking, K2.5 and K2.6 about 595 GB), CL-21, CL-22 and CL-23 (today `df` shows 198 GB free, 90% used; the dossier gives a formula).
- CL-09: partly rejected, and the rejection is justified. vLLM's docs say -tp 8 causes '8x KV cache duplication' for MLA.
- Only partly fixed:
  - CL-04: the reword is right, but the new S137 evidence misdescribes the GGUF as a 20-layer truncation; it keeps 2 layers.
  - CL-06: '0731' is named throughout, but F1 still mixes in an April-checkpoint run (S96, 2026-06-14) and a Vision-Exp run (S108). The '284B/13B on its card' line cites the 0731 card, which does not state it. The 156 GB MXFP4 recipe does not name the Vision-Exp file.
  - CL-08: the 43.2% attribution is fixed. However, 2.82×/1.93× are still presented as speedups when they are read-bandwidth ratios. The 5.85 GB/s 'purpose-built floor' is stated as fact in section 1, though the only macOS streamer the dossier quantifies implies about 3.4 GB/s.

lens:
ARITHMETIC (round 2). I recomputed the rebuilt bandwidth model (A2-A7), every fit label, every tokens/s estimate (in memory, streamed, pruned, top-k, K6), the KV sizes (A9), the prefill model and its ds4 check, the Mac disk and download tables, the H100 HBM/KV arithmetic, and the GPU-hour budgets for G1-G5. I also checked each round-1 AR finding against the revision. Independent inputs, all gathered on 2026-10-15:
- **GGUF tensor tables.** I wrote my own parser and read the headers over HTTP range requests (no weights downloaded) for 9 files: antirez V4 Flash IQ2XXS-0731 (ds4 Q2), antirez V4 Flash Vision-Exp MXFP4, antirez GLM-5.3 IQ2_XXS, antirez GLM-5.3-Flash Q2 and Q4_K, Unsloth V4-Flash-0731 UD-IQ3_XXS (4 shards) and Unsloth GLM-4.6 UD-TQ1_0. Tensor sizes come from offset differences. Parser and summariser: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kevinliu-repos-cotcodec/122e47b9-8f46-4266-97af-e75214712991/scratchpad/arith2/gguf_hdr.py and summ.py.
- **Configs.** deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash and -0731 config.json.
- **Local status.** `headroom status --json`, `sysctl hw.memsize` and `vm_stat`.

The Kimi K2.6 Q2, K2-Thinking TQ1_0, R1, Qwen3-235B and gpt-oss rows were already measured independently by two parties (round-1 verifier and this revision), and their numbers agree, so I did not re-parse them. All other arithmetic was recomputed from the dossier's stated inputs.

problems.claim: A3 table rows 'V4 Flash 0731, ds4 Q2 (antirez IQ2XXS)': pool 76.10, routed 1.78, spine 7.56, total 9.34 GB, and 'V4 Flash Vision-Exp, MXFP4 experts (ds4)': pool 143.75, routed 3.37, spine 7.56, total 10.93. A3 parameter count 'V4 Flash: 277.7B total, 13.0B active'. Corrections log AR-01: 'V4 Flash ds4 Q2 reads 9.34 GB per token, not 9.57, because its 1.99 GB MTP block is not used in ordinary decode.'
problems.problem: This is a regression of a correct round-1 finding. The antirez files contain no MTP block; ds4 ships MTP as a separate file. The 1.99 GB the revision excluded is blk.42, the last of V4 Flash's 43 trunk layers, so both ds4 rows drop one real layer (about 2.4% of bytes). The same revision counted all 43 blocks for the Unsloth 0731 UD-IQ3_XXS file (its 9.22 GB matches my parse exactly), so the V4 Flash rows are internally inconsistent. Because of the undercount, the dossier's own parameter count (277.7B) disagrees with the card's 284B, which conflict #12 treats as a source disagreement.
problems.evidence:
- **Header parse, antirez V4 Flash IQ2XXS-0731** (86,720,111,488 B): `deepseek4.block_count` 43, blocks blk.0-42 only, no blk.43.
- **Layer 42 is a trunk layer:** blk.42 has 34 tensors totalling 1.994 GB, including attn_compressor_*, an indexer and 256 routed experts. `compress_ratios` has 44 entries; entry 42 is 4 and entry 43 (the MTP layer) is 0.
- **Config:** deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 config.json gives num_hidden_layers 43 and num_nextn_predict_layers 1. The MTP layer is extra.

problems.problem:
There are three arithmetic problems.
1. **ds4's appends contradict the no-hit model.** Both appends, and the GLM-5.3-Flash cold prompt unless compute is under 0.7 s, run faster than one no-hit pass plus compute even at the 10.6 GB/s ceiling. So ds4's managed cache serves prefill hits, or ds4 overlaps reads with compute, or it reads faster than 10.6 GB/s. Only the V4 Flash 8K cold prompt fits the stated model.
2. **The ds4-style row contradicts the dossier's own description of ds4.** The row adds pass time to compute time, but conflict #10 says ds4 overlaps reads with compute. With overlap, the 30K whole-prompt case is compute-bound.
3. **Fractional passes.** The micro-batch rows count 30,000/4,096 = 7.32 passes. The partial 1,328-token batch still touches about 100% of experts (1 − (1 − 8/384)^1328 ≈ 1), so the count is 8 passes, and 59 for 512-token batches.
problems.evidence:
- **GLM-5.3-Flash Q4_K** (171.23 GB pool): one no-hit pass takes 16.15 s at 10.6 GB/s.
  - The 1K append took 1,024/104 = 9.8 s, below even that one pass.
  - The 2K cold prompt took 2,048/121 = 16.9 s. Adding compute at V4-like in-memory rates (about 2.6-3.3 s) gives at least 18.8 s.
- **V4 MXFP4 4K append** (corrected 147.17 GB pool): measured 4,096/263 = 15.6 s. No-hit minimum: 13.9 s + 5.2 s of compute = 19.1 s. With hits only on the uncached 54.6 GB: 10.3-16.5 s, which fits.
- **Kimi 30K prompt, recomputed:**
  - with overlap, whole prompt: 30,000 / max(31.2, 162) = 185, and 30,000 / max(56.6, 300) = 100, so **100-185 tokens/s, 2.7-5.0 min**;
  - no-hit, 8 passes of 4,096: **40-73 tokens/s, 6.9-12.5 min**;
  - managed cache (first pass cold, later passes read only the uncached 252.4 GB): 4,096-token batches **46-83**; 512-token batches **10.5-19** (no-hit 8.2-15).
problems.fix:
1. Replace 'Both fit' with: 'Cold prompts fit about one full pass; warm appends are faster than any no-hit pass, so ds4's managed cache does serve prefill hits.'
2. Give the ds4-style row as 84-185 (no overlap to full overlap).
3. Give the 4,096 row as 40-73 tokens/s (6.9-12.5 min) with no hits, and up to 46-83 with a managed cache.
4. Section 1's '3-12 minutes' becomes about 2.7-12.5 minutes.

problems.claim: A7: 'all other work stopped: an 88 GB budget − 9.3 GB of non-routed weights = 78.7 GB, which is 23.8% of the 331.1 GB pool', against 'today's free memory: 57.6 GB − 9.3 − 2.3 to 4.4 (KV at 32K) − 3 = 41-43 GB'. The same 88 GB − non-routed rule sets the cache in K1 (64 GB), K3 (80.3 GB), D2 (77.1), D3 (76.9) and Q5 (82.5).
problems.problem: The two cache budgets use different rules. The 'today' line subtracts KV and 3 GiB of buffers. The 'all other work stopped' line, which every headline streaming row uses, does not. A7 itself defines the cache as free memory − resident non-routed weights − KV − about 3 GB of buffers, so the stopped-case shares are 2-6 points too high.
problems.evidence:
Applying A7's own rule to the 88 GB budget:
- **K2.6 Q2:** 88 − 9.34 − (2.30 to 4.35) − 3.22 = **71.1-73.1 GB**, which is **21.5-22.1%** of 331.14 GB, not 23.8%.
- **Other rows** shrink by the same 5.5-7.6 GB (KV + buffers). For example, D3 becomes about 69-72 GB, or 54-55% of 129.1 GB, not 59.6%.

At the A7 brackets the h ranges barely move, so the tokens/s ranges change by a few percent. The rule is still inconsistent.
problems.fix: Use one rule for both cases: cache = budget − non-routed − KV at the stated context − 3 GiB. Restate the stopped-case shares (K2 about 22%, K3 about 31%, D2 about 33%, D3 about 54%, Q5 about 35%), or state that the 88 GB is already net of KV and buffers, and say where 88 GB comes from.

problems.claim: A10 and section 1: '57.6 GB free (45%)'; 'Claude sessions held 81.1 GB, Chrome 24.4 GB'; A7 'today's free memory: 57.6 GB'; 'Any model that needs more than about 57 GB means stopping other work today.'

problems.claim: A6 flash-moe back-test: 'with B set to its measured 3.4 GB/s, A6 predicts 5.5-5.7 tokens/s. It measured 4.36, so the real time per token is 25-32% longer than A6.' Not applied to the Kimi estimates.

B = 3.4 GB/s is derived from flash-moe's own measured I/O time, so the SSD term (144.9 ms) is exact by construction. The whole miss is in A6's memory/compute term. The remaining time per token is 2.2-2.9 times A6's memory term, which matters for the cache-heavy Kimi cases.

- **flash-moe time split:** measured 229.4 ms − 144.9 ms of SSD time = 84.5 ms, against an A6 memory term of 7.2 GB / (188-244 GB/s) = 29.5-38.3 ms. That is 2.2-2.9 times.

problems.fix: Report the flash-moe residual as '2.2-2.9 times A6's memory term', and give the downside case for the Kimi row: about 2.0-4.5 tokens/s with flash-moe-like overhead, against 2.5-5.8 without it.

problems.claim: Row K1: 'Streamed with the shipped BF16 spine (35.3 GB per token) ... about 0.8-1.7'. Section 4: 'SGLang's DP attention does not fit: every GPU would hold the full BF16 attention weights (about 12.3 GB, from A8) in only about 11 GB of free memory.' These are three small inconsistencies with the dossier's own rules. None changes a conclusion.

- **DP attention:** under TP8 each GPU already holds 1/8 of the attention weights (1.54 GB), so DP attention adds about 10.8 GB, not 12.3, against 11.06 GB free. That leaves about 0.25 GB with no KV room, so the conclusion holds but the comparison is off.

problems.evidence:
- **K1:** 21.14B × 4.5/8 = 11.89 GB routed, plus 10.55B × 2 = 21.1 GB spine, gives 33.0 GB. The tokens/s range is unchanged at 0.8-1.7.
- **DP attention:** 6.17B × 2 = 12.34 GB, minus 12.34/8 = 1.54 GB, is 10.8 GB, against 10.3 GiB = 11.06 GB free.

That is about 14 KB per token, or 0.43 GiB at 32K, plus about 0.14 GB of KDA state. Total 89.88 + 0.43 + 0.13 + 3 = 93.4 GiB, which is 'Yes' up to about 150K context.
problems.fix:

- **DP attention:** say 'adds about 10.8 GB per GPU against 11 GB free, leaving no KV room'.
- **F3:** label it 'Yes by A10 (93.4 GiB at 32K); ds4 advises modest context', or explain why ds4 needs more memory.

round1_fixes_confirmed:
Of the 20 round-1 arithmetic (AR) findings, 17 are fixed correctly, 2 are fixed with errors and 1 has a small inconsistency. CL-09, NV-04, NV-05 and NV-09 are also fixed correctly.

- **AR-11 and CL-09.** 79.6 GiB per GPU / 684 GB in total; 69.3 GiB used and 10.3 free; 2.3 / 6.3 GiB free at utilisation 0.90 / 0.95; 46-92K tokens (BF16) and 92-183K (FP8); 4-8 or 8-17 sequences of 11K; 0-2 of 64K.

- **AR-15 to AR-20.** All check. Ratios 4.33, 1.71-1.81, 1.22-1.35; 1.924 bits; K6(i) 95.0 GB / 93.6-95.5 GiB / 18-24 tokens/s; K6(ii) 108.4 GB / 106.1-108.0 GiB / 23-30 tokens/s; 2-GPU limit about 150 GB; 3 and 5 GPUs; 16.4 GiB at 1M.

- **NV-04, NV-05, NV-09 and the budgets.** 0.075-0.55M tokens per GPU-hour; 6.4-11.2M tokens per setting; G2 13-51, G4 18-137, G5 29-314, G1 54-306 (Stage 1 25-73). Each line sums correctly.
- **Downloads.** About 3.04 TB in total, 6.8 h at 1 Gb/s.

**Fixed with errors:**
- **AR-01 regression.** The V4 Flash ds4 Q2 and Vision-Exp rows drop trunk layer 42, which the revision called a nonexistent MTP block. The round-1 9.57 GB was correct.
- **AR-14.** The top-k range mixes old and new parameters. The correct gains are +28-30% (top-6) and +76-87% (top-4).

**Small inconsistencies:**

- **AR-06 ds4 check.** 'Both fit' is false for the warm appends; the micro-batch rows use fractional passes.
verdict:
The rebuilt arithmetic is mostly sound, and the headline conclusions stand:
- Kimi streams on this Mac at about 1.4-5.8 tokens/s, as an estimate;
- a 753B GLM 5.3 streams at a measured 4.1-5.1 tokens/s;
- DeepSeek V4 Flash about 2-bit is the best measured in-memory option.

**Checks that hold.** I recomputed every streamed, in-memory, KV, fit, disk, H100 and GPU-hour figure, and nearly all match their stated inputs to rounding. Five new tensor-table rows I parsed myself match the dossier exactly: GLM 5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash Q2 and Q4_K, GLM-4.6 and V4-0731 UD-IQ3_XXS.

**Problems still open:**
1. **Regression of a correct round-1 number (minor in effect).** The two antirez V4 Flash rows exclude blk.42 as an "MTP block". It is a real trunk layer: config num_hidden_layers is 43, and MTP ships as a separate file. Correct values: ds4 Q2 reads 9.57 GB per token, Vision-Exp MXFP4 reads 11.19 GB, and the model is 284.3B / 13.27B.
   - Effects: V4 calibration e = 0.61 / 0.57 / 0.55 / 0.46; F1 estimate 30-39; S2 cache share 63%.
2. **G1's research question (major).** Its build range (62.5-75% pruned, 2-2.7 bits) mostly breaks its own 100 GB bound. At 2 bits or more, only 75% pruning fits; 62.5% needs 1.91 bits or fewer.
3. **Top-k gains (minor).** They should be +28-30% and +76-87%, not 26-30% and 69-84%.
4. **Prefill (minor).** ds4's warm appends are faster than any no-hit pass, so "both fit" is false. Because the dossier says ds4 overlaps reads with compute, the ds4-style Kimi row could be 100-185 tokens/s. The 4,096-token micro-batch row with 8 whole passes is 40-73.
5. **Memory budgets (minor).** The stopped-case cache omits the KV and buffers that A7's own rule subtracts (about 22% of the pool, not 23.8%). Headroom's 57.6 "GB" is 57.6 GiB = 61.8 GB.

None of these changes the answer to Kevin's question. Fix items 1-3 before the numbers are reused in pre-registrations or the G2 emulator validation.
